entry.title: Institutional Response Tracker
entry.content:
From Courts to Checkpoints

The Anderson Localization analysis showed that captured judges create disorder in the judicial lattice. Cases that enter cannot propagate to a fair hearing.

But courts are not the only institutional checkpoint. Michigan has layered accountability structures: credentialing bodies, oversight commissions, authorizers, professional discipline departments, and law enforcement agencies. Each exists to catch what the others miss.

The question this page answers: When the same verified evidence is submitted to multiple institutional checkpoints simultaneously, which ones act and which ones don’t?

The answer reveals whether the accountability system functions or whether the disorder extends beyond the courts into the institutions designed to oversee them.

The Model

Every institutional checkpoint is a lattice site. Evidence arrives like an electron. Either the institution transmits it forward (investigation, action, referral) or it absorbs and traps it (closure, dismissal, non-response).

If every checkpoint absorbs, the system is fully localized. No accountability can propagate.

The measurement is simple:

InputWhat Was Submitted
SubjectBrian Roderick Banks: 9 criminal convictions (SID 2029469K), unauthorized use of “J.D.” credential, operation of two DPSCD-authorized charter schools
EvidenceICHAT criminal record, LARA corporate filings, MOECS credential audit, academic performance data (3% math proficiency), financial records ($4.9M revenue, 72.67% extraction to Purpose Group LLC), campaign finance data
FormatVerified public records, structured for independent verification
Sitedetroit.primals.eco

The same evidence package. Multiple institutions. Measure the output.

The Data

Checkpoint Response Table

This table is updated as responses arrive. Each row documents the institutional output for the same evidentiary input.

#InstitutionDepartmentFiledResponseDaysResult
1Michigan Dept. of EducationEducator Excellence20222022–Cleared with conditions
2Detroit Public Schools CDBoard of DirectorsJul 2025Jul 2025–Authorized second school
3State Bar of MichiganUPL Dept. (File 26-UP-51)Aug 2026Sep 30, 2026~30Administratively closed
4State Bar of MichiganUPL (2nd complaint)Sep 2026–PendingAwaiting response
5Baker CollegeHuman ResourcesOct 2026Oct 5, 2026<2Permanently severed
6Attorney Grievance CommissionProfessional discipline (x7)Sep-Oct 2026–PendingInvestigations pending
7Judicial Tenure CommissionJudicial conductSep 2026Sep 2026~5Investigations opened
8Central Michigan UniversityCharter authorizationPending––Notification staged
9MDE (Round 2)Credential re-examinationPending––Notification staged
10Detroit Inspector GeneralMunicipal oversightPending––Complaint staged

Key Observations

The only institution that acted in under 48 hours was a private employer with no regulatory obligation.

Baker College reviewed the same evidence that Michigan’s credentialing body, authorizing district, and professional bar department reviewed. Baker permanently severed ties. The regulatory bodies either cleared him, authorized him, or closed the complaint.

The UPL Department’s stated reason for closure: “Does not meet the standards set by the Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee to pursue this matter further.” The subject uses “J.D.” in professional communications, holds no bar admission in any jurisdiction, and operates a school named “School for Law and Public Service.”

The UPL Department’s stated alternative: “You may have other remedies available to you.”

The UPL complaint was the first of several submitted as the scope of the unauthorized credential use became clear through the investigation. Additional complaints remain pending and will be updated here as responses arrive.

The Asymmetry

Michigan’s system demands active defense from individuals:

  • A parent must file a motion and appear at a hearing to see their own children
  • A citizen must file an affirmative defense within 14 days to contest a personal protection order
  • A pro se litigant must meet the same procedural standards as a licensed attorney
  • A victim of assault must obtain and serve their own police report
  • A custody case requires the responding parent to affirmatively request the investigation the filing parent opted out of

But when a citizen uses the system’s own accountability tools:

  • A UPL complaint against a 9-time convicted felon using “J.D.” is closed as not meeting standards
  • An administrator certification for a habitual offender is granted with conditions
  • A second charter school is authorized for an operator whose first school ranks in the bottom 3% statewide
  • A police report filed at the scene of an assault requires the victim to drive to the precinct to retrieve it

The system enforces process against citizens aggressively. It declines to enforce against its own members passively.

This asymmetry is not incidental. It is the localization.

When the disorder in the lattice extends from the courts into the oversight bodies, the accountability signal has nowhere to propagate. Every checkpoint absorbs it. The individual is left with “other remedies available to you,” which means: the system has told you it will not help.

The Measurement Continues

This page is a living document. As institutional responses arrive, the table updates. Each response or non-response is a data point in the same experiment.

The question is not whether any single institution failed. Institutions make judgment calls. The question is whether the pattern of non-response across multiple independent checkpoints reveals structural localization rather than individual discretion.

When the same evidence produces action from a private college in 48 hours and produces closure from a state regulatory body in 30 days, the comparison is the finding. No editorial interpretation is required.

This is Anderson Localization measured in institutional responses rather than court assignments. The physics is the same: disorder prevents propagation. The measurement is how deep the disorder goes.

All submissions are documented. All responses are recorded as metadata. All claims are verifiable against public records. See Legal Protections for the First Amendment and fair comment framework.

Related: The pattern of institutions that ignore boundaries extends beyond Michigan oversight bodies. See Signal — Public Record of Automated Access for evidence of the same dynamic in corporate AI systems that access this investigation site: some check the rules and comply; others read the rules and scrape anyway.

entry.title: FBI Wiretap Target List — Beeckman Affidavit (2017)
entry.content:
Source

In December 2017, court records in the Eastern District of Michigan were accidentally unsealed. Celia Washington’s attorney, filing a motion to suppress wiretap evidence in her criminal case, included FBI Special Agent Robert Beeckman’s application to continue wiretapping against more than a dozen people.

The records were reported by:

  • MLive — Accidentally exposed court records reveal new names in corruption probe (Dec 2017)
  • WXYZ Detroit — New names of public officials emerge in federal corruption investigation (Dec 2017)
  • Detroit News — original reporting on the unsealed Beeckman affidavit

The investigation is linked to the federal corruption case against Gasper Fiore (US v. Fiore, 16-cr-20732), owner of Boulevard & Trumbull Towing, who pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit federal program bribery.

Complete Target Subject List

All 18 individuals named as “Target Subjects” in the Beeckman wiretap application:

#NameKnown RoleCase Status
1Gasper FioreOwner, Boulevard & Trumbull Towing. Built a towing empire across Metro Detroit through bribery. Debarred from Detroit contracts 20 years (2018-2038).Convicted — pled guilty, 16-cr-20732, bribery conspiracy. 21 months. Wore a wire for the FBI post-conviction.
2Romel CasabFormer owner of the Packard Plant (Detroit). Beeckman wrote evidence showed “crimes involving corruption” but insufficient for charges.Indicted Jan 2016 — marijuana distribution, drug facility (29100 Northline Rd, Romulus), firearms. Also filed Kassab v. Detroit (2:22-cv-12307) re: marijuana licensing.
3Paul OttOwner of Gene’s Towing Inc and City Wide Towing Inc. Companies alleged by Detroit OIG to be fronts for Fiore. Debarred 7 years (2018-2025). Sued Detroit (2:19-cv-10853) claiming city improperly used wiretap affidavit — dismissed.Not federally charged. Debarred.
4Shane AndersOwner of Star Towing (Monroe) and Area Towing (Taylor). FBI COOPERATOR — NOT corrupt. Told FBI that Mayor Sollars forced him to use Fiore for heavy tows. FBI cleared him as not a target (Mar 8, 2018). His cooperation led to FBI raid on Sollars. Filed whistleblower lawsuit against Sollars and MSP.NOT charged. Cleared. His company Area Towing filed the civil case (2:19-cv-10989) that produced the FBI wiretap files containing Banks conversations.
5Gabriel LelandDetroit City Councilman. Was dating Jennifer Fiore (#11) while voting on Fiore towing contracts.Convicted — state plea, bribery.
6Vonda EvansWayne County 3rd Circuit Judge (retired).JTC suspension. Named in wiretap. Not federally charged.
7William “Bill” WildTowing/auto salvage operator — Hi-Way Auto Equipment (Taylor), Bill Wild Enterprises (Wayne), City Auto Storage (3400 E Lafayette, Detroit), Phil’s Towing, Independent Auto Wreckers of Detroit. Connected to Ferrous Processing & Soave Enterprises.Not publicly charged. Same industry as Fiore — competitor or associate in towing bid-rigging.
8Alberta Tinsley-TalabiRetired state representative (aka Jewel Ware).Named in Beeckman affidavit: “crimes involving corruption” but “evidence so far has not been sufficient to bring federal charges.”
9Morris JosephFormer Detroit Police officer. Involved in towing operations — sued in Anjorin v. City of Detroit (2:16-cv-10893) for directing Boulevard & Trumbull to tow vehicles from resident’s property. Metro Times identifies him as “ex-Detroit cop.”Not federally charged.
10Benny NapoleonWayne County Sheriff.Named in Beeckman affidavit alongside Tinsley-Talabi and Casab: “crimes involving corruption” but insufficient evidence. Died Dec 2020 (COVID).
11Jennifer Marie FioreDaughter of Gasper Fiore. Debarred 15 years (2018-2033).Not federally charged. Fox 2 reported she was dating Councilman Leland while he voted for Fiore contracts.
12Brian Roderick BanksResigned state representative, charter school operator. Recorded on Fiore’s wiretapped phone.Not federally charged. 9 state convictions (SID 2029469K). Subject of this investigation.
13Michael Patrick GormanRole in investigation not publicly identified.Not publicly charged.
14Assad Ibrihim TurfeDeputy Wayne County Executive (promoted Sep 2022). Was Chief Assistant to County Executive Warren Evans when named on wiretap. Started as Wayne County Sheriff’s deputy (2002), rose to youngest lieutenant, then Chief of Staff, now #2 in Wayne County. Dearborn native. Honored by Arab American community. FBI had probable cause he was “engaged in the payment and receipt of bribes.”Not charged. Now runs Wayne County.
15Louay Malakey HusseinManager of Nationwide Towing Inc (owned by brother Hussein “Sam” Hussein). Employer: Mayflower Enterprises, “President of Operations.” Northville, MI. $272,750 in political contributions (TransparencyUSA) to gubernatorial, PAC, and legislative campaigns. Detroit OIG investigated Nationwide for “hunting” stolen vehicles, above-market rates, cash-only payments. Brother owns MetroTech Collision.Not criminally charged. Subject of OIG investigation. Massive political donor in towing industry.
16Michael Irvin LucasWorked at B&G Towing in Detroit. Married to Jessica Lucas (née Fiore), daughter of Gasper Fiore. Jessica ran Boulevard & Trumbull day-to-day operations, debarred 10 years. Lucas is Fiore’s son-in-law — family member embedded in towing operations.Not publicly charged. Source: Detroit News.
17Celia WashingtonFormer DPD Deputy Chief of Police and legal adviser to the Chief. Oversaw DPD towing permits, licensing, and rotations. Accepted $4,000 cash from Fiore + $800 bar tab at birthday party + car arrangement + free oil changes from another tower. Met Fiore privately at Coldstone and bars, gave him personal email to avoid detection. Her attorney Arnold Reed’s motion to suppress is what accidentally exposed this entire target list.Convicted — pled guilty Jan 2018 to bribery conspiracy. Sentenced Apr 2018: 12 months + $2,500 fine + 2 years supervision.
18Robert Ray NicholsonRole in investigation not publicly identified.Not publicly charged.

The Fiore Towing Empire — Debarment Map

The Detroit Office of Inspector General debarred the following individuals and companies in connection with the Fiore corruption investigation (OIG Debarment List, June 2024):

#EntityDebarmentPeriod
1Gasper Fiore20 yearsMay 2018 – May 2038
2Jennifer Fiore (daughter)15 yearsMay 2018 – May 2033
3Joan Fiore (ex-wife)15 yearsMay 2018 – May 2033
4Javion & Sam’s Towing Service Inc15 yearsMay 2018 – May 2033
5Jessica Lucas (daughter)10 yearsMay 2018 – May 2028
6Boulevard & Trumbull Towing Inc20 yearsMay 2018 – May 2038
7Paul Ott7 yearsMay 2018 – May 2025
8Gene’s Towing Inc7 yearsMay 2018 – May 2025
9City Wide Towing Inc7 yearsMay 2018 – May 2025
10Anthony Thomas7 yearsMay 2018 – May 2025
11B & G Towing7 yearsMay 2018 – May 2025

Also on the same OIG debarment list: Bobby W. Ferguson (20 years, March 2013 – March 2033) — the Kilpatrick co-conspirator.

Beeckman’s Assessment

FBI Special Agent Robert Beeckman wrote in the wiretap request:

“Evidence has been gathered showing that crimes involving corruption have been committed by some of the target subjects, including Tinsley-Talabi, Napoleon and (Romel Casab, former owner of the Packard plant in Detroit). However, those investigations have been pending for months or years and the evidence so far has not been sufficient to bring federal charges.”

What This Means

The FBI had active wiretap surveillance on Brian Roderick Banks as part of a multi-county corruption investigation centered on towing contracts, bid-rigging, and bribery of public officials. Banks was recorded on Gasper Fiore’s phone discussing matters that drew FBI scrutiny.

Of the 18 target subjects:

  • 3 have been convicted (Fiore, Leland, and Washington was charged)
  • 3 were named as having committed corruption but without sufficient evidence for charges (Tinsley-Talabi, Napoleon, Casab)
  • 1 has 9 state convictions and operates two charter schools extracting millions in public funding (Banks)
  • 7 remain publicly unidentified in terms of their role in the investigation

The wiretap investigation is part of the same FBI Detroit field office operation that produced Operation Northern Hook (Spivey, Sollars, Jones convictions), the Macomb County corruption probe (23+ convictions including Eric Smith, Dean Reynolds, Anthony Marrocco), and the EAA/DPS school corruption probe (Snapp, Thornton, Norman Shy, 12+ principals).

The EAA Connection

The same FBI field office and the same AUSAs (J. Michael Buckley and Frances Lee Carlson) prosecuted:

  1. Glynis Thornton — EAA school vendor corruption (M.A.D.E. tutoring kickbacks)
  2. Kenyetta Wilbourn-Snapp — EAA principal corruption ($58K kickbacks, Maserati with GUCCI1 plates)
  3. Norman Shy — DPS vendor corruption ($2.7M fraud, 12 principals, 13 years)
  4. Bert Johnson — State senator ghost employee scheme (Thornton was FBI cooperator CW-1)

Thornton cooperated in the EAA probe, which led to the DPS principal probe, which was investigated by the same office running the Fiore wiretap that captured Banks. The school corruption ecosystem and the political corruption ecosystem share the same investigative apparatus — and the same geography.

The EAA was dissolved June 30, 2017. Its schools returned to DPSCD. DPSCD later authorized Banks’s Purpose Charter Academy — with board member Sherry Gay-Dagnogo voting to approve. Gay-Dagnogo then received a 10-year appointment as City Ombudsman.

Former EAA principal Snapp told the court: “Payoffs were part of the education culture in Detroit.”

Banks extracts 72.67% of school revenue through a self-dealing LLC. Same culture. Different mechanism. Same city. Same FBI field office.

Verification

  • Fiore case: PACER — 16-cr-20732 (E.D. Mich.)
  • Area Towing civil case: PACER — 2:19-cv-10989 (E.D. Mich.)
  • Leland plea: State court records, widely reported (Free Press, Detroit News)
  • Casab indictment: Detroit News, Jan 14 2016
  • Johnson case: DOJ press release, Apr 11 2017, Case No. 17-20233
  • Thornton/Snapp: CBS Detroit, Free Press
  • Norman Shy: AP, Free Press
  • Dean Reynolds: Washington Times/AP, 6th Circuit No. 19-1146

All claims sourced to federal court records, DOJ press releases, and named journalism. See Sources for database access instructions.

entry.title: Every Person Named in Banks's Book — Network Map from His Own Words
entry.content:
What This Page Is

Brian Banks wrote a book. He named people. He described relationships. He confessed to behaviors — his own and others’. Every word is a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — his own published statement, admissible against him in pending litigation.

This page catalogs every person named in the book, identifies who they are using public records, and documents the relationships and behaviors Banks described in his own words.

Fair use notice: All excerpts are used for criticism, commentary, and public-interest reporting under 17 U.S.C. § 107. See the companion analysis for the full fair use framework.

The Judges — Three “Mentors” Who Are Sitting or Retired Jurists

Judge Denise Langford Morris — 42 References

Role per Banks: “my mentor” Actual role: Banks’s felony sentencing judge in Oakland County Circuit Court (~1999). Now retired. Wrote the book’s foreword.

Banks describes a relationship that progressed from judge-defendant to personal mentorship to campaign labor to credential endorsement:

  1. Sentenced Banks leniently (1-year probation, 6 months tether)
  2. Told Banks: “you need to get back in school and go to someone’s law school!” — while knowing his felonies would bar admission
  3. Met Banks for lunch at Brandy’s restaurant on Telegraph in Pontiac through mutual friend Roeiah
  4. Discussed her morning docket with civilians at the restaurant: Banks writes that “Judge Langford Morris was describing her morning docket to Roeiah and the other young lady and the various cases that she had heard.” A sitting judge describing active cases she heard that morning to non-lawyers at a restaurant.
  5. Invited Banks back to her courtroom and paraded him to staff
  6. Attended MSU Law BLSA events at Banks’s invitation
  7. Treated Banks to dinner when he “graduated from law school” — along with “several other judges”

  9. Wrote the foreword to a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.” — endorsing the credential fraud of the felon she sentenced

What Banks confesses she did:

  • Discussed active cases with civilians in a restaurant (Canon 2, Rule 2.10 — Judicial Statements on Pending Cases)

Banks writes: “Retired Judge Vonda Evans and I became friends almost sixteen years ago. Vonda and I met through a mutual attorney friend one summer while hanging out in downtown Detroit.”

Luckily, we both got our stuff together and Tenisha graduated and received her bachelor’s and law degrees. She then became an assistant prosecuting attorney even with felonies and misdemeanors.”

A sitting judge who Banks states had “felonies and misdemeanors” and “spent a month or two in jail.” Banks published this. It’s his party admission about a member of his network. Her sister operates his school. They still live one street apart.

Behaviors Banks Confesses Others Committed

These are not accusations. These are descriptions published by Brian Banks in his own book.

1. A Sitting Judge Discussed Active Cases in a Restaurant

“Judge Langford Morris was describing her morning docket to Roeiah and the other young lady and the various cases that she had heard.”

Location: Brandy’s restaurant, Telegraph Road, Pontiac, Michigan. Approximate date: ~2006-2007 (Banks says “Seven and a half years” after 1999 sentencing).

A sitting Oakland County Circuit Court judge discussed her morning docket — specific cases she heard that same day — with civilians at a restaurant. This violates:

  • Canon 2, Rule 2.10 — Judicial Statements on Pending and Impending Cases
  • Canon 1, Rule 1.2 — Promoting Confidence in the Judiciary
  • MRPC 3.5 — if any attorney was present

2. A Sitting Judge Developed a Personal Relationship with a Former Defendant

Banks describes the progression: sentencing → chance reconnection through Roeiah → restaurant lunch → courtroom visits → law school event invitations → graduation dinner → Supreme Court campaign volunteering → book foreword.

This is an improper ex parte personal relationship between a judge and a former felony defendant she sentenced.

3. A Sitting Judge Endorsed Credential Fraud via Book Foreword

Langford Morris wrote the foreword to a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.” while knowing:

  • She sentenced him for multiple felonies
  • Those felonies prevented bar admission
  • He was using “J.D.” as a professional credential without a license

As a former assistant U.S. Attorney (Eastern District of Michigan), Langford Morris knows precisely what “J.D.” means without bar admission. Her endorsement of the book is an endorsement of the credential fraud.

4. “Several Other Judges” Celebrated His “Law Graduation”

“When I graduated from law school, Judge Langford Morris and several other judges and friends treated me to dinner to celebrate.”

Multiple unnamed judges personally celebrated a nine-time convicted felon’s law school graduation — a defendant whose felonies they knew would prevent bar admission.

5. Judges Vonda Evans and Cylenthia Miller Arrived at a Family Hospital

Two sitting judges responded to a personal family medical crisis — Banks’s grandfather’s hospitalization and death. This is documented personal relationship, not professional interaction.

6. A Sitting Judge Had “Felonies and Misdemeanors”

Banks writes about Judge Tenisha Yancey:

“Tenisha ended up having some troubles of her own which caused her to spend a month or two in jail… She then became an assistant prosecuting attorney even with felonies and misdemeanors.”

Banks published this about a sitting Wayne County judge. Whether true or false, it is his own party admission about a network member.

7. “Prominent People” Knowingly Purchased Stolen Goods

“Some of the people who were buying the items from us were prominent people and they knew that the items were obtained through illegal means.”

Banks confesses that unnamed “prominent people” knowingly received stolen merchandise from his organized retail theft operation. He does not name them. They are unindicted co-conspirators described by the defendant himself.

8. Gay-Dagnogo and Judge Evans at Hospital Night

“That night, my friends, Sherry Gay-Dagnogo and Judge Vonda Evans…”

A state representative and a sitting judge were at Banks’s personal family crisis event. This is the personal network that later voted for PCA’s charter (Gay-Dagnogo) and endorsed Banks’s campaigns.

What This Means

Brian Banks did not just write a memoir. He published a network diagram with names, relationships, titles, and institutional affiliations — all in his own words, all admissible as party admissions, all permanently available at ISBN 173575403X.

Every person named in the acknowledgments chose to be associated with “Brian Banks, J.D.” — a credential that does not exist. Every judge named as a “mentor” accepted a personal relationship with a nine-time convicted felon. Every licensed attorney named as a friend tolerated the unauthorized use of “J.D.” credentials in their professional network.

The book is not a memoir. It is an org chart.

entry.content:
Fair Use Notice

This page is a public-interest commentary and analysis of “It Had 2 Happen: The Agony of Success” (ISBN 173575403X, True Vine Publishing Co., 2020) by Brian Banks, J.D. All excerpts are used under the fair use doctrine, 17 U.S.C. § 107, for purposes of criticism, commentary, and public interest reporting.

Four-factor fair use analysis:

  1. Purpose: Non-commercial criticism, commentary, and public-interest journalism. This site has no advertisements, no donations, no monetization. The purpose is to protect 362 children attending schools operated by the book’s author.
  2. Nature of the work: A published autobiography — the lowest tier of copyright protection. Self-published, commercially available, and branded with credentials the author does not hold.
  3. Amount used: Selected excerpts only, each accompanied by original commentary and cross-referenced against independently verifiable public records. No chapter is reproduced in full.
  4. Market effect: None. Amazon ranked this book #2,637,193 in Kindle Store (per M.L. Elrick, Detroit Free Press, 2022). This commentary does not substitute for the original work.

The book’s own copyright page states: “a reviewer may quote brief passages in a review.” This is a review.

The book is also a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Banks’s own published statement, offered against him as a named party in pending litigation (Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ, Ingham County Circuit Court). Every word is admissible. No foundation required beyond authentication. The ISBN authenticates it.

Banks has no copyright claim that survives fair use. An attempt to suppress this analysis would constitute a SLAPP action against protected criticism of a public figure (former State Representative) regarding matters of profound public concern (credential fraud affecting public schools).

The Book

FieldValue
TitleIt Had 2 Happen: The Agony of Success
Author“Brian Banks, J.D.”
Copyright© 2020 Brian Banks
PublisherTrue Vine Publishing Co., P.O. Box 22448, Nashville, TN 37202
ISBN-10173575403X

Pages184
Also published“Brian Banks, J.D. at Smashwords” — ebook, $9.99

Self-claimed rank“#1 Bestseller”
Actual Amazon rank#2,637,193 in Kindle Store (Elrick, 2022)

The author is credited as “Brian Banks, J.D.” on the cover, copyright page, and all retail listings. The State Bar of Michigan returns zero results for “Brian Banks.” He was denied bar admission on Character & Fitness due to nine criminal convictions. The J.D. degree is real. The right to use it as a professional credential is not. 📄 Documented

The Credential Fraud Begins on the Cover

Banks’s biography page — the final section of the book — reads:

“Honorable Brian R. Banks, M.Ed., J.D.”

Three false credential claims in six words:

  1. “Honorable” is a title reserved for judges and elected officials. Banks resigned from the legislature in 2017 after his ninth conviction. He is not a sitting official.
  2. “J.D.” implies a licensed legal practitioner. Banks has never been admitted to any bar.
  3. The biography states he aspired to “become a prominent attorney and, then, sit on the bench as an officer of the court” — admitting the exact goal he has been fraudulently representing as achieved.

The biography further claims:

“He has earned a Juris Doctor with a Concentration in Criminal Law from Michigan State University College of Law”

True. He earned the degree. He was never licensed to practice.

“Mr. Banks is a highly sought-after consultant, educator, organizer, assistant, community, political, legal mind and now, an author.”

“Legal mind.” Not “attorney.” Not “licensed.” The phrasing is a carefully constructed near-claim — close enough that readers assume licensure, vague enough to defend as technically truthful. This is how credential fraud works when the person committing it went to law school.

The Network Map — Banks Named Them All

The acknowledgments section of the book is a complete social network map, written by the node himself. Every name below appears in Banks’s own words. 📄 Documented

Judge Cylenthia LaToye Miller“my mentor” — appears at his grandfather’s hospitalSitting 3rd Circuit Judge. PCA Board President (LARA Entity 900072324). Appears 7 times. JTC complaint filed.

Three sitting judges called “my mentor” in a published book by a nine-time convicted felon. Two appeared at his family hospital bedside. One served as his felony sentencing judge, then developed a personal relationship, then endorsed the credential fraud by writing the foreword.

The Confessions — Banks in His Own Words

Confession 1: A Decade of Felonies

Banks writes in the introduction:

“Every decision that I made, from roughly 1993 to 2003, impacted me for years.”

He dates his criminal activity as a ten-year span — broader than previously documented in court records. 📄 Documented

Confession 2: Identity Theft and Organized Retail Fraud

Banks provides a detailed written description of his criminal operation:

“One of my so-called ‘friends’ taught me… how to obtain fraudulent credit cards. We obtained the cards in other people’s names, used them until they were maxed out and then paid the cards off with checks from accounts with insufficient funds.”

“Our crimes grew from small gift cards to opening up large credit cards at designer department stores. We would purchase designer handbags, clothing, and other items with the fraudulent credit cards and then later sell it all for cash.”

“Some of the people who were buying the items from us were prominent people and they knew that the items were obtained through illegal means.”

The author describes: identity theft, credit card fraud, check fraud, fencing stolen goods to named “prominent people,” and an organized retail theft operation. Published under oath of authorship.

Confession 3: Habitual Lying

“No matter how many times I used his credit cards without his permission, he was still there to support me. No matter how many times I told a lie, he still stood by my side.”

“No matter how many times I told a lie” — a party admission of habitual dishonesty, published in his own book, available at ISBN 173575403X. 📄 Documented

Confession 4: The Suburban Reality

The “raised in Detroit” narrative is the foundation of Banks’s public persona. His book dismantles it.

Book ClaimWhat It Reveals

“They took me out of public school and put me in a private school called Lutheran East High School”Lutheran East is at 20100 Kelly Road, Harper Woods, MI 48225 — a suburb
Told Morse podcast (ep85) he attended “Denby High School”Different school entirely. Denby is a Detroit public school. Lutheran East is a suburban private school.

Grandfather produced $60,000 cash for bailFamily had significant resources
Visited University Liggett in Grosse Pointe Woods in 8th gradeNOW lives in Grosse Pointe Woods (1968 Severn Rd)
“every school that I attended from kindergarten to high school, was in this district”HD-1 includes Harper Woods — confirming suburban schooling

Confession 5: The Plan — In Writing

From the introduction:

“graduate from college, attend law school, graduate again, become a prominent attorney and, then, sit on the bench as an officer of the court.”

And from the biography:

“Brian saw a clear path — graduate from college, graduate from law school, become a prominent attorney, and then sit on the bench as an officer of the court.”

The plan was always to become a lawyer and a judge. The nine felony convictions prevented both. Instead of abandoning the plan, Banks simply pretended he achieved it.

The Langford Morris Relationship — Judicial Corruption in 42 References

Judge Denise Langford Morris appears 42 times in this 184-page book. She is the central figure in Banks’s “Revelation Day” narrative. Here is what Banks himself documented: 📄 Documented

  1. Banks’s felony case was assigned to Langford Morris in Oakland County Circuit Court (~1999)
  2. She was the “only black judge on the bench” in Oakland County at the time
  3. Banks’s defense attorney was Mr. Condino
  4. Langford Morris gave Banks a lenient sentence: 1-year probation, 6 months tether, court costs, fines, restitution
  5. Banks represented himself in a motion to remove his tether — his first taste of “practicing law”
  6. Langford Morris removed the tether and told him: “you need to get back in school and go to someone’s law school!”
  7. Banks cultivated a personal relationship through mutual friend “Roeiah” (33 mentions) — met Langford Morris for lunch at Brandy’s restaurant on Telegraph in Pontiac
  8. At that lunch, Langford Morris was discussing her morning docket with civilians
  9. Banks told her he was “currently in my first year of law school”
  10. Banks visited her courtroom and she paraded him to her staff
  11. When Banks “graduated from law school,” Langford Morris and “several other judges” treated him to dinner
  12. Banks volunteered on Langford Morris’s Michigan Supreme Court campaign
  13. Langford Morris wrote the foreword for a book branded “Brian Banks, J.D.”

A sitting judge: sentenced a felon leniently, encouraged him to pursue a legal career she knew his felonies would bar, developed an improper personal relationship, discussed active docket matters with civilians, campaigned using his volunteer labor, and endorsed his credential fraud via the foreword of a published book.

All documented in the defendant’s own words. All admissible under MRE 801(d)(2)(A).

The Holland Unit — “Permanent Fixture in Our Family”

Joseph Holland appears throughout the book under the name “Joe.” Banks’s own words establish Holland as a member of his domestic/economic unit: 📄 Documented

Book ReferenceWhat It Proves
“my best friend and brother… You’ve now become a permanent fixture in our family”Domestic unit, not business relationship
Present at Banks’s master’s graduation (“my grandfather, my mother, my brother, and my friends, Angie, Beverly, and Joe”)At every major life event
When FBI arrived, Banks’s first call was to Holland — they went to attorney Ben Gonek’s office togetherThey share legal crisis response
“Joe and I returned to the funeral home a day or so later so Joe could give my grandfather one last haircut”Holland is providing personal grooming services for the deceased grandfather
Judges Vonda Evans and Cylenthia Miller arrived at the grandfather’s hospitalThe judges and Holland are at the same family crisis event

Holland has three felony convictions of his own. He served as treasurer of Banks’s PAC. He shares Banks’s mailing address. The book confirms what the public records already show — this is a single domestic/economic unit operating under the “Brian Banks, J.D.” brand.

The Yancey Revelation — Same Street, Same Schools, Now a Judge

Banks writes about Tenisha Yancey:

“One of my elementary school friends was Tenisha. Tenisha and I lived on the same street and went to elementary and high school together.”

“Currently, we live one street over from each other”

“This is the same Tenisha who succeeded me after I resigned from office.”

Judge Tenisha Yancey — a sitting Wayne County judge:

  • Lived on the same street as Banks growing up
  • Attended the same schools (elementary and high school)
  • Still lives one street over in Grosse Pointe Woods
  • Took Banks’s State Representative seat when he resigned after his ninth conviction
  • Her sister operates Banks’s PCA school

Banks also writes that Tenisha had “felonies and misdemeanors” and still became an “assistant prosecuting attorney.” 📄 Documented

Any case heard by Judge Yancey involving Banks, Holland, PCA, MacDowell, or any entity in this network is compromised by an undisclosed lifelong personal relationship documented in the defendant’s own published autobiography.

The BMF Connection — “To This Day, Toni and I Remain Close”

Banks writes about his step-aunt:

“my Step-aunt Toni got into some trouble with her then boyfriend, ‘T.’”

“my aunt was a part of the internationally known group called ‘Black Mafia Family’ better known as ‘BMF’”

“To this day, Toni and I remain close.”

“Toni” is Tonesa Welch — BMF Defendant #22 in USA v. Flenory et al. Banks’s biological father is also a BMF defendant. Banks admits an ongoing relationship with a convicted member of one of the largest drug trafficking organizations in American history.

Tonesa Welch published her own book: The Black Mafia Family. The same pattern — hundreds of pages, zero victims named, zero accountability.

The AG Prosecution — Holland Is First Call When the FBI Arrives

Banks describes the day federal agents appeared:

“I called Joe, who was at work, and told him what had just taken place and asked him to meet me at the lawyer’s office at 11 a.m.”

When the FBI arrives, Banks’s first call is Holland. They go to attorney Ben Gonek’s office together. They leave together.

“Soon after, Joe and I left the conference room”

The Attorney General’s prosecution resulted in Banks’s guilty plea to false statements/financial condition, his forced resignation from the Michigan House on February 6, 2017, and his ninth criminal conviction.

The book refers to this prosecution six times. Banks frames it as political persecution. The public record shows a guilty plea.

The Funeral Home Connection — Does It Lead to Clora?

Banks writes:

“I had been working part-time at a funeral home for number of years”

Major C. Clora Jr. is the current PCA Board Assistant Treasurer and owner of Clora Funeral Home in Detroit. Clora attended Wayne State’s Mortuary Science program. Banks was at Wayne State and considered mortuary science as his major before switching to Criminal Justice.

If Banks worked at Clora Funeral Home, their connection predates everything — going back 20+ years. Banks’s appointment of Clora to the PCA board was not random. It was a decades-long personal relationship. ? inference

The Numbers Don’t Lie

MetricBook’s FramingPublic Record
Criminal history“journey,” “setbacks,” “not-so-smart decisions”9 convictions (6 felony, 3 misdemeanor), 5 courts, 1998–2016
Education“from GED to a law degree”Degree is real. Bar admission denied. Never licensed.
Self-description“Honorable Brian R. Banks, M.Ed., J.D.”Not honorable. Not licensed. Used “J.D.” commercially.
Book sales“#1 Bestseller”#2,637,193 in Kindle Store (Elrick)
School performance“ensuring all children have access to quality education”MacDowell: 3% math proficiency, bottom 3% statewide
Revenue“my business has been doing quite well”72.67% of per-pupil funding extracted to Purpose Group LLC
Apology to victims(none)Zero victims named in 184 pages. Zero accountability.

The Apology That Never Comes

Across 184 pages and approximately 55,000 words, Brian Banks does not:

  • Name a single victim of his financial crimes
  • Acknowledge harm caused by his forgery, identity theft, or fraudulent check schemes
  • Disclose his bar denial — the “J.D.” appears on the cover without disclosure
  • Address the performance record of the schools he now operates
  • Express genuine remorse — every setback is framed as character development
  • Use the word “sorry” as an apology — it appears only in contexts of self-pity

The word “lie” appears once — as a confession:

“No matter how many times I told a lie, he still stood by my side.”

Why This Book Is Evidence

Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Party Admissions

Banks is a named party in Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ. Every word in this published book is admissible against him as a party-opponent statement. It is not hearsay. No foundation is required beyond authentication — and authentication is trivial for a published book with an ISBN.

What This Means:

UseRule
Any factual claim is his own binding statementMRE 801(d)(2)(A)
The book self-authenticates as a published workMRE 901(b)(6)
Any inconsistency between the book and testimony is impeachmentMRE 613
The credential branding is itself evidence of unauthorized practiceMCL 600.916
Prior acts showing plan, scheme, identity, intentMRE 404(b)
Specific instances of conduct for truthfulnessMRE 608(b)

Cost of the evidence: $9.99 (ebook) + $25.00 (paperback) = $34.99

Evidentiary yield: 184 pages of binding party admissions, a complete network map, criminal confessions, impeachment material for every future proceeding, and a published record of credential fraud that cannot be scrubbed, edited, or denied.

The Book Is Not a Memoir. It Is a Confession.

Brian Banks wrote a book under the name “Brian Banks, J.D.” and published it while unlicensed. He listed himself as “Honorable” on the biography page. He named every major node in his institutional network in the acknowledgments. He confessed to a decade of criminal activity in his own words. He documented improper judicial relationships with three sitting judges. He described his economic unit with a three-time convicted felon as “a permanent fixture in our family.”

Then he called it a “#1 Bestseller” when Amazon ranked it 2.6 millionth.

Everything about this man is a fraud — including his book sales.

Verify Everything
